      • logAndThrow

        public static <T extends Exception> T logAndThrow​(org.slf4j.Logger log,
                                                  T exception)
                                           throws T extends Exception
        You can use that if you want to log a message and throw an exception with the very same message as an error, to avoid constructing the message twice. throw ExceptionUtil.logAndThrow(new XYException("something is wrong with " + argument), LOG); The throw is not necessary, but informs the compiler about the thrown exception.
        Type Parameters:
        T - the exception type
        Parameters:
        log - where the exception should be logged
        exception - an exception
        Throws:
        T - the exception e is thrown.
        T extends Exception

      • sneakyThrowException

        public static RuntimeException sneakyThrowException​(@NotNull
                                                    @NotNull Exception exception)
        Throws the given exception even if it's a unchecked exception, without needing to declare this. Please use sparingly and with caution and for a good reason, as this is, as it says, sneaky. Do declare the thrown exception on the method that's using this construct inside. You can't catch this exception unless you use catch(Exception) or declare it on a method calling this. You can use it like throw sneakyThrowException(e); to inform the compiler that we never continue.
        Parameters:
        exception - the exception to throw
        Returns:
        does never return - just for coding clarit

      • sneakExceptions

        @NotNull
public static <ARG,​VALUE> @NotNull Function<ARG,​VALUE> sneakExceptions​(@NotNull
                                                                                   @NotNull ExceptionThrowingFunction<ARG,​VALUE,​Exception> function)
        Returns a function that calls the original function and might sneakily throw even checked exception without declaring them - for use with Streams. You can (cautiously!) use this with Java 8 style stream methods without using complicated exception handling, but please remember to declare the thrown exceptions on the method! That'd look for example like: list.stream().map(ExceptionUtil.sneakExceptions(Node::getPath).collect(Collectors.toList());
        Type Parameters:
        ARG - argument type of the function
        VALUE - return type of the function
        Parameters:
        function - the function to call
        Returns:
        the result of calling the callable

      • callAndSneakExceptions

        @Nullable
public static <T> T callAndSneakExceptions​(@NotNull
                                           @NotNull Callable<T> callable)
        Calls the callable and sneakily throws even checked exception without declaring them. You can (cautiously!) use this with Java 8 style stream methods without using complicated exception handling, but please remember to declare the thrown exceptions on the method! That'd look for example like: list.stream().map((n) -> ExceptionUtil.callAndSneakExceptions(() -> n.getPath())).collect(Collectors.toList());
        Type Parameters:
        T - the type parameter
        Parameters:
        callable - the callable
        Returns:
        the result of calling the callable
        See Also:
        sneakExceptions(ExceptionThrowingFunction)
